answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks when reputation grows like a garden tended over seasons, not bought in bulk: newcomers lock a refundable copper stake, then complete small verifiable tasks checked by randomly assigned peers, earning signed receipts hash-chained to the previous one. A fresh identity entering the tundra of anonymous accounts starts with no credit and must pay real work over time; one forged receipt breaks the chain and slashes the deposit, so buying throwaway identities buys nothing.
